title: Import templates and scope card do not state the decided rule that historical sign-ups need their Deal and Operator in Salesforce first (including deals that are not in the current Airtable snapshot)

jira.summary: Build data import templates — Sign Up, Referral, Secondary Referral, Player
jira.quote: Build import templates for the four objects above so WagerTech can populate and send back clean data for ingestion.

**Decide:** historical Sign-Ups, yes or no; historical redeposit and payout data; US Deals and Deal Rep Assignments; the 26 Deals with no Source; whether the legacy Google Sheets keep getting data during the switch-over.

what_differs: On 8/11 the team agreed that a historical sign-up import needs a version of the related deal (and operator) in Salesforce, otherwise the sign-ups have no relationships. Airtable holds only a current snapshot. WAGR-477 and WAGR-470 do not state this dependency, the Deal/Operator key on the Sign Up template, or the need to load historical or inactive deals first.
suggested_action: Add acceptance criteria to WAGR-477: the Sign Up template carries the Deal key (External Deal ID) and the Operator/Partner keys, and the load order is operators/partners, deals (including historical or inactive deals that historical sign-ups reference), then players, then sign-ups and referrals. Add the inactive-deal question to WAGR-470.
